title: S3 buckets, object keys, and prefixes
hook: An S3 bucket is a globally unique container; object keys are flat strings where prefixes like logs/2026/ organize data without real folders.

blocks.text: Amazon S3 stores objects in buckets within an AWS Region. Bucket names are globally unique across all AWS accounts. Each object is identified by a key — a UTF-8 string that can include slashes to simulate folder hierarchy. Prefix is the substring before the delimiter for ListObjectsV2 filtering. There is no atomic rename — copy then delete.

entries.plainDefinition: Regional container with globally unique name holding objects.
Unique string identifier for object within bucket.
Leading portion of key used for list filters and lifecycle.
Character (usually /) grouping common prefixes in list response.

blocks.text: Key layout affects lifecycle rules, IAM condition keys, and query performance. Multi-tenant SaaS often embeds tenantId in prefix. Wrong mental model of folders causes access and listing cost issues.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: flat keys, prefix convention, ListObjects with delimiter for console tree view. Design keys for lifecycle and IAM s3:prefix conditions.

snippet.label: Create bucket and upload object
snippet.code:
aws s3 mb s3://my-app-data-prod-123456789012-ap-south-1
aws s3 cp ./report.csv s3://my-app-data-prod-123456789012-ap-south-1/tenants/acme/reports/2026/report.csv
snippet.explanation: Bucket name must be globally unique. Key includes full logical path.

snippet.label: List objects by prefix
snippet.explanation: Delimiter groups pseudo-folders. Avoid listing entire bucket in hot paths.

snippet.label: CloudFormation S3 bucket
snippet.code:
DataBucket:
  Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
  Properties:
    BucketName: !Sub "${AWS::AccountId}-app-data-${AWS::Region}"
    PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
      BlockPublicAcls: true
      BlockPublicPolicy: true
      IgnorePublicAcls: true
      RestrictPublicBuckets: true
snippet.explanation: Block public access by default. Bucket name often includes account and region.

snippet.label: IAM condition on prefix
snippet.explanation: Restrict principals to tenant prefix using session tags or IAM paths.

blocks.title: Runtime and deployment parallels
rows: readdir — cheap locally, costly at scale in S3
No native glob — prefix filter only
glob npm package on local FS

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Treating console folders as real directories for permissions. Listing entire bucket in a loop — expensive and slow. Special characters in keys without URL encoding.

blocks.text: S3 Express One Zone for low-latency high-QPS within AZ — different bucket type. How to prove it in production: S3 Storage Lens top prefixes by request count, and CloudWatch NumberOfObjects per prefix via inventory.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying S3 has folders like POSIX directories gets rejected. Strong answer: flat keys, prefix design, ListObjects with delimiter, IAM on prefix.

interviewTakeaways: Bucket names are globally unique; keys are flat strings.
Use prefix layout for tenant, env, and lifecycle — not real folders.
ListObjectsV2 with prefix/delimiter — never scan whole bucket in app hot path.
60s: Flat keys. Prefix tenant/env/date. List with prefix. Separate buckets for hard isolation.
Follow-up: how do you secure multi-tenant keys?
commonPitfalls: Believing folders enforce access — weak; IAM and bucket policy enforce access.
Strong answer: prefix in key + IAM condition + optional bucket per tenant.
Full bucket ListObjects in polling loop — cost and throttling.
Unencoded spaces and special chars breaking CloudFront origin paths.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Use string template for S3 keys — path.join uses OS separators. Keys always use forward slash.
Paginate with ContinuationToken — like async iterator over large arrays, do not assume single response.
